title: Starburst Galaxy M82
caption: The starburst galaxy M82, imaged by the WIYN 3.5-meter telescope and the Hubble Space Telescope
credit: Mark Westmoquette (University College London), Jay Gallagher (University of Wisconsin-Madison), Linda Smith (University College London), WIYN//NSF, NASA/ESA

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: This color-coded picture shows M82, the archetypal starburst galaxy. Its stellar disc runs horizontally and is where its intense star formation takes place. Rising perpendicular to the disc is a galactic superwind of ionized gas, driven by the energy released by the burst of star birth.

A starburst galaxy forms stars much faster than usual. So many massive young stars live and die so quickly that their combined winds and explosions blast gas out of the galaxy, producing the outflow. Dust lanes are visible in the central part of the superwind on both sides of the disc, shown at varying angular resolution.

That mix of resolutions comes from the data sources. The image merges observations made by Kitt Peak's WIYN 3.5-meter telescope with data from Hubble's WFPC2 camera. The data are being used to study how structures within M82 connect to its superwind.

understand.summary: The image combines WIYN 3.5-meter and Hubble WFPC2 data in visible light. In the WIYN data, purple shows glowing hydrogen (hydrogen-alpha) together with ionized nitrogen, and green shows ionized sulfur. In the Hubble data these colors show hydrogen-alpha and nitrogen separately.
understand.eye: The colors are coded to particular glowing gases rather than showing natural color, so the superwind stands out in a way the eye would never see.

explore: The image was first shown at the Essential Science in Hubble's Final Years symposium, held at the Space Telescope Science Institute in May 2004. Kitt Peak's WIYN 3.5-meter and 0.9-meter telescopes are run by a consortium made up of the University of Wisconsin, Indiana University and Yale University, together with the National Optical Astronomy Observatory.
alt: A horizontal galaxy disc with a purple and green outflow of gas rising above and below it, laced with dark dust.
